sources.quote: Word stress in Dela falls on the penultimate syllable of the root. Since each vowel is a syllable nucleus, it is the penultimate segmental vowel that carries the stress. Roots with two metrical feet have secondary stress on the initial syllable.

sources.citation: Tamelan, Thersia Magdalena. 2021. A grammar of Dela: an Austronesian language of Rote, eastern Indonesia. PhD thesis, Australian National University. hdl:1885/250953
sources.quote: 'Word stress in Dela falls on the penultimate syllable of the root. Since each vowel is a syllable nucleus, it is the penultimate segmental vowel that carries the stress. Roots with two metrical feet have secondary stress on the initial syllable. A metrical foot in Dela consists of a stressed syllable followed by an unstressed syllable. Affixes, partial reduplication, enclitics (including sentence/phrasal enclitics) and paragogic vowels are extrametrical, which means they are not counted in stress assignment, and stress does not shift. Stress is mainly realised by pitch, intensity and duration
sources.note: The deciding source itself; cited as read but no copy was held on file. fetched sources now; quote confirmed verbatim at sec 2.2.5 p.36.

sources.citation: Tamelan, Thersia M. & I Wayan Arka. 2021. Adjuncts at the syntax-prosody interface in nominal structures in Dela. In Butt, Findlay & Toivonen (eds.), Proceedings of the LFG'21 Conference, 264-284. Stanford: CSLI Publications. hdl:1885/294455
sources.quote: 'In Dela, word stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the root and each vowel is a syllable nucleus. The root or stem is typically disyllabic, forming a trochee... Prefixes, genitive and plural enclitics are extrametrical—they do not influence word stress, or in other words, stress does not shift.'
sources.note: Only other Dela-specific prosody work found; independent restatement of root-penultimate trochaic stress with extrametrical prefixes/enclitics. fetched sources now; confirms.
